paper_title: ASyMOB Algebraic Symbolic Mathematical Operations Benchmark
caption: belowskip=0pt : Effect of equivalence-type perturbations. Note the substantial drop in success rate for most models, even when performance on the seed set is high.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the success rates (in percentage) of various large language models on the ASyMOB benchmark under different types of equivalence perturbations, with the x-axis listing the models and the y-axis representing the success rate from 0% to 100%. The models are arranged from left to right in a non-alphabetical order, likely reflecting their performance on the seed set, with Gemini 2.5 Flash (Code) and Gemini 2.0 Flash (Code) showing the highest seed success rates near 100%, while models like GPT-4o and Nemotron-Super-v1 show much lower seed success rates, around 50% and 40% respectively. Each model has five grouped bars corresponding to different perturbation types: 'Seed' (dark blue), 'Equivalence-One-Easy' (medium blue), 'Equivalence-One-Hard' (light blue), 'Equivalence-All-Easy' (very light blue), and 'Equivalence-All-Hard' (pale blue), as indicated in the legend. The bars consistently show a progressive decline in success rate from the seed set to the hardest perturbation type, with the 'Equivalence-All-Hard' bars being the shortest for all models. For example, Gemini 2.5 Flash (Code) drops from ~98% on the seed to ~65% on 'Equivalence-One-Hard' and ~60% on 'Equivalence-All-Hard', while GPT-4o drops from ~50% to ~10% and ~5% respectively. The chart visually emphasizes that even models with high seed performance suffer substantial performance degradation under equivalence perturbations, particularly when multiple or harder equivalences are applied. The bars are not sorted by any specific criterion other than model name, and no special visual emphasis (e.g., shading or annotation) is applied to any particular bar.
